source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten primary or authoritative references: Valiant's BSP paper, Baudet's JACM DOI record, Bertsekas-Tsitsiklis book and 1989 paper, Tseng-Bertsekas-Tsitsiklis SIAM DOI record, the NeurIPS SSP paper, Dijkstra-Scholten's archival manuscript, official MPI 5.0 PDF/nonblocking-collective page, and current PETSc KSP convergence documentation. Eight returned HTTP 200 locally. ACM and SIAM DOI endpoints returned HTTP 403 but their bibliographic and abstract records were reviewed through indexed publisher results. PETSc was reviewed through its current documentation index; shell curl could not resolve petsc.org. Claims are scoped to the cited models and do not assert universal asynchronous convergence.

evidence: Definitions consistently distinguish synchronous generation k, asynchronous event t, component read version tau_ij(t), delay d_ij(t), bounded staleness s, contraction q, epoch e, partition generation g, and component version v_i.
Fixed-point, residual, activity/passivity, and quiescence terminology remains distinct from runtime completion, collective completion, and empirical performance.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked domains, inequality directions, logical clocks, norms, residual qualification, version terminology, and synchronous/asynchronous distinctions.

evidence: Recomputed bulk states [8,7,0,0], [8,7,6,0], [8,7,6,5], then stability; recomputed in-place updates 1,2,3 reaching the same fixed point.
Recomputed Exercise 1: 10*(0.8)^8=1.6777216 and ceil(ln(.01)/ln(.8))=21.
python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-089 passed exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code in artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-089/report.json.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Integer propagation is exact; the chapter explicitly denies that this finite example proves general asynchronous convergence or performance.

evidence: Re-derived the contraction step ||F(x^k)-F(x*)||<=q||x^k-x*|| and induction bound q^k||x^0-x*||.
Checked synchronous x^(k+1)=F(x^k) against asynchronous component updates using explicitly versioned arguments tau_ij(t).
Checked that the BSP cost expression and nested-box/fairness discussion are labeled models or theorem routes rather than universal laws.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Banach-style synchronous reasoning is intentionally not extended to arbitrary mixed versions; asynchronous conclusions are conditional on a matching theorem.

evidence: Reviewed q=0, q approaching 1, zero residual, NaN/Inf, nonunique fixed points, one worker/component, starvation, unbounded finite delay, stale/reordered/duplicate/cross-epoch messages, and compound non-atomic reads.

Reviewed weak MPI progress, inconsistent collective order, early buffer reuse, outstanding-resource exhaustion, queue pressure, local inactivity with in-flight work, recursive-versus-true residual drift, and premature rank exit.

Reviewed numerical reorder, ill-conditioning, repartition, checkpoint/replay, lost worker/message, ordinary MPI failure, denial/resource attacks, telemetry disclosure, power-grid state estimation, and radiotherapy optimization.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Covers mathematical, schedule, memory, communication, termination, resource, numerical, failure, security/privacy, operations, and high-stakes boundaries.

evidence: Every update is attributable to a run/epoch/partition/component/version and one authoritative update rule; stale owners and cross-epoch traffic cannot mutate current state.

Atomicity, fairness, freshness/delay, duplicate/loss, collective order, request/buffer lifetime, queue bounds, and numeric-error assumptions are mapped from implementation events to the chosen theorem.
Stopping requires an admitted global residual and passive workers with no unaccounted work/messages; publication follows drain/freeze, final validation, and legal communication completion.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked operator, schedule, protocol, termination, checkpoint, rollback, and publication invariants end to end.

evidence: The synchronous contraction proof states the complete-space, mapping, norm, q<1, fixed-point, and exact recurrence premises.
The schedule-admissibility argument requires a problem-specific asynchronous theorem and explicitly names fairness, delay/freshness, atomicity, step-size, perturbation, and message assumptions.
The termination argument separates numerical stopping from distributed quiescence and accounts for reactivation and in-flight credits/messages before output.
proof_review.notes: No barrier removal, atomic access, bounded average latency, local residual, empty queue, passing snippet, or faster test is treated as a universal correctness/convergence/performance proof.

evidence: Exact contraction algebra, conditional theorem routes, protocol obligations, cost models, and empirical measurements are separately labeled.
The executable model disclaims MPI, staleness, floating arithmetic, performance, failure, and general convergence evidence.
Power-grid and radiotherapy cases enumerate named review roles and explicitly claim none.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Scientific/clinical validity, safety, privacy/security, recovery, portability, and scalability remain outside the demonstrated integer model.

evidence: Snippet verification reproduced the exact synchronous and immediate-update sequences and fixed-point check.

The experiment requires identical problem/operator/precision/resources/tolerance/oracle and tests balanced/skewed placement, slow workers, delay/reordering/duplicates, progress, queue limits, schedules, failures, and restore.

Required metrics cover time-to-valid-solution, component fairness, useful/discarded updates, staleness, traffic, queues, residual trajectory, synchronization/progress/checkpoint costs, resource use, numerical difference, timeout, and divergence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter reports no unperformed cluster, MPI implementation, fault-recovery, scientific, clinical, security, or safety experiment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed fixed-point foundations, BSP, safe overlap, asynchronous version models, theorem matching, consistency/version protocols, residuals, quiescence, convergence/error evidence, performance experiments, failure/recovery, operations, security, and high-stakes limits.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed MPI weak progress and collective order, request/buffer lifetime, epoch/version/owner fencing, duplicate/reorder policy, bounded queues/backpressure, enforceable staleness/fairness, exact/global residual checkpoints, termination credits, checkpoint/restore, telemetry/runbooks, conservative fallback, and time-to-valid-solution decisions.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes four synchronization regimes before optimization, derives the synchronous bound, makes asynchronous assumptions explicit, supplies one deterministic model, counters eighteen misconceptions, gives ten varied examples through power-grid use, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers including radiotherapy.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematics, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external Valiant/BSP, ACM/JACM/SIAM/NeurIPS, MPI Forum/PETSc/runtime/library, formal verification, distributed-systems, numerical/optimization/scientific, cluster/network/accelerator/OS, fault-tolerance, power-systems/protection/control, radiation-oncology/medical-physics/dosimetry/imaging, cybersecurity/privacy, operations/SRE, data-quality/regulatory/certification, ethics, accessibility/human-factors, or independent safety review is claimed. The chapter proves neither an arbitrary asynchronous implementation's convergence/termination, MPI correctness, reproducibility, fault recovery, performance, portability, scalability, nor grid-state/clinical validity, privacy, approval, or deployment safety. ACM and SIAM DOI endpoints denied automated curl with HTTP 403, and shell curl could not resolve PETSc; those records were reviewed through publisher/current documentation search indexes.
